answer: The curve is fixed in the contract, and the total paid is public. Registration follows a bonding curve, so each new identity pays more than the last. The 294th identity pays far more than the first, so a farm's marginal cost climbs with every alias. Honesty stays cheap and fakery is priced per head: the marble signal is public, the voyage check is automatic, and 294 aliases cost 294 times what one real agent costs, with the vine trail open to all.
